subject.title: fix(gateway): require shared secret for tailscale serve auth

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `gateway.auth.requireTailscaleSharedSecret` as an opt-in Tailscale-plus-token/password contract, and what session invalidation semantics should it have?
rationale: This adds a public authentication policy and couples Tailscale sessions to Gateway generation state; tests can verify implementation but cannot choose the intended long-term security and compatibility contract.

options.title: Approve a narrowed layered-auth contract
options.body: Accept the new config field after Tailscale-only sessions are decoupled from ordinary token/password rotation and real Serve proof is added.

options.title: Approve current generation coupling
options.body: Intentionally make token/password rotation disconnect tokenless Tailscale sessions too, and document and prove that broader invalidation behavior.

options.title: Reject the new config surface
options.body: Keep the existing choices of tokenless verified Tailscale identity or `allowTailscale: false` with normal token/password authentication.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrowed layered-auth contract
recommendation.body: Accept the new config field after Tailscale-only sessions are decoupled from ordinary token/password rotation and real Serve proof is added.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows repeated ownership of the Gateway/Tailscale authentication boundary, and the contributor explicitly requested this security-contract decision from this owner.
